Note: This is the Spot Price, not the NYMEX Futures price. If the EIA does not report a price for this specific date (e.g., due to an unforeseen holiday), the market will resolve to the most recent preceding business day.

# Research report 1 of 2

I couldn't read the EIA or FRED pages: every page fetch was refused by the proxy, so everything below comes from search-result summaries. WTI ended the week of Aug 28 at about $83.2 to $83.4, almost exactly on the $83 line, and prices were swinging hard.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on EIA's Cushing WTI spot series (RWTCD), which FRED mirrors as DCOILWTICO. I could not open the [EIA page](https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/RWTCD.htm) or FRED, so I can't report the latest official daily spot value or its date.
- The spot price usually stays close to the front-month NYMEX contract (October 2026, CLV26), but it is a separate number.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. Futures are within about $0.20 to $0.40 of the threshold.
- 2026-08-28 (Fri): WTI fell $0.36 to $83.17 and lost about 5% on the week. Brent was $89.32. [Ship & Bunker](https://shipandbunker.com/news/world/944386-iranian-resolve-strained-but-traders-faith-in-its-control-of-hormuz-causes-5-weekly-loss-for-oil)
- 2026-08-28: Trading Economics had crude at $83.40, down about 4% on the week. An earlier version of its story that day had oil below $83. [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/crude-oil/news/579248)
- 2026-08-28: A Vantage CFD feed showed WTI at $83.79 at 10:25 GMT+8. [Vantage](https://www.vantagemarkets.com/market-analysis/brent-wti-crude-oil-price-chart-august-28-2026/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-28: Traders see the Iran situation as a sanctions fight more than a threat to physical supply. Iran and Oman agreed a revenue-sharing framework for the Strait of Hormuz, though Tehran says that does not mean an immediate reopening. Goldman puts Persian Gulf exports at about 15 to 16 mb/d, against 22 to 24 mb/d before the conflict. Washington reportedly won't revive the terms of the June deal that collapsed. [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/crude-oil/news/579248)
- 2026-08-26: WTI was about $80.09 in the morning, down about 2.8% from the prior settlement of $82.36. It was the third straight losing session, on hopes Hormuz restrictions would ease. [EnergyNow](https://energynow.com/2026/08/oil-prices-slide-on-growing-hopes-for-strait-of-hormuz-reopening/)
- 2026-08-25: US officials confirmed the Navy had cleared mines from the strait's shipping lanes. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis)
- 2026-08-11: EIA's August STEO raised its 2026 Brent average forecast from $82 to $87. It assumed Hormuz restrictions would last until August, and it expects US commercial crude stocks to stay below the five-year low through 2026. [longportapp](https://longportapp.cn/news/295569247), [EIA PDF](https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/archives/aug26.pdf)
- 2026-08-10: WTI rose 4% to back above $82 after Iran ruled out direct talks with the US. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/10/oil-prices-today-brent-wti-hormuz-trump-iran.html), [Oil & Gas 360](https://www.oilandgas360.com/oil-climbs-4-after-steep-weekly-loss-as-uncertainty-over-hormuz-reopening-mounts/)
- 2026-08-07: Crude settled at $78.2, down more than 7% for the week. [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/crude-oil/news/573883)
- 2026-08-03: WTI fell about 5% to around $80 on progress in US-Iran talks. [World Oil](https://worldoil.com/news/2026/8/3/oil-drops-as-u-s-iran-signal-progress-on-hormuz-discussions/)
- 2026-07-31: WTI settled at $84.67, with Brent at $90.12. [EnergyNow](https://energynow.com/2026/08/oil-price-rises-after-iran-says-it-stops-ships-in-hormuz/)

## 4. Base rates and volatility
- Recent levels: $84.67 (Jul 31), about $80 (Aug 3), $78.2 (Aug 7), above $82 (Aug 10), $82.36 (Aug 25), about $80.1 intraday (Aug 26), about $83.2 to $83.4 (Aug 28).
- One tracker gives an August range of about $75.22 to $87.83, a $12 spread in a single month. [worldoilmonitor](https://worldoil.com/wti)
- Moves of 4% to 8% in a week and 3% to 5% in a day have been common. That is roughly $3 to $7 a week at current prices.
- The resolution date is 8 trading days away. At this volatility, the typical move over that horizon is several dollars, much larger than the gap between today's price and $83.
- The trend is lower, with Hormuz de-escalation behind it, but rebounds have been sharp whenever talks hit trouble (Aug 10, for example).

## 5. Other forecasts
- EIA's August STEO projects a 2026 Brent average of $87. I could not find its WTI figure.

- About Sept 6: an OPEC+ meeting of the eight-country group, if it follows the usual early-month schedule. I could not confirm a date or agenda.
- Sept 7: US Labor Day. There will be no EIA spot price that day.
- Ongoing: the US-Iran and Iran-Oman Hormuz talks, tanker traffic data from Kpler and Goldman, any further attacks on ships, and sanctions moves.

# Research report 2 of 2 (written independently)

I couldn't open any page directly because the proxy refused every fetch, including FRED, Fortune, CNBC and Wikipedia. Everything below comes from search-result summaries, so treat the exact figures as needing a check.

## 1. Resolution source
- Resolves to EIA / FRED series DCOILWTICO (Cushing WTI spot, daily). I couldn't fetch FRED, so **I don't have the latest official spot value.** [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DCOILWTICO)
- 2026-08-28: The front-month WTI futures contract (October, CLV26) settled at **$83.40**, down $0.13. The Cushing spot price usually tracks the front-month settlement within a few cents, so spot was probably close to $83.40. That is my inference; I have not seen the EIA figure. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/28/oil-on-track-for-weekly-loss-even-as-iran-tensions-simmer.html), [Barchart](https://www.barchart.com/futures/quotes/CLQ26)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. WTI is sitting almost exactly at the $83 threshold (about $83.40 on 08-28), and resolution is 8 trading days away. Labor Day (09-07) is a market holiday.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-28: Both benchmarks fell for the week (WTI about -4%, Brent more than -5%). Brent settled at $89.31. Traders weighed stalled U.S.-Iran talks against some crude moving through the Strait of Hormuz. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/28/oil-on-track-for-weekly-loss-even-as-iran-tensions-simmer.html)
- 2026-08-28: An intraday snapshot had WTI at $83.79 and Brent at $90.07, with Hormuz flows rising. [Vantage](https://www.vantagemarkets.com/market-analysis/brent-wti-crude-oil-price-chart-august-28-2026/)
- 2026-08-26: WTI fell about $2.08 to roughly $80.29, its lowest since 08-10, after Iran restarted talks with Oman on managing the Strait. Both benchmarks had dropped more than 3% on 08-25. [Oman Observer](https://www.omanobserver.om/article/1195123/business/energy/oil-prices-fall-on-iran-oman-talks-to-reopen-strait-of-hormuz), [NST](https://www.nst.com.my/amp/business/economy/2026/08/1505171/oil-prices-slip-iran-oman-talks-fuel-hopes-us-iran-peace-deal)

- 2026-08-18/19: WTI was around $85 after a vessel was hit in the Strait on 08-17, and Trump threatened to bomb Oman. [Angel One](https://www.angelone.in/news/commodities/crude-oil-prices-rise-as-us-iran-peace-hopes-fade-and-supply-risks-grow-august-18-2026), [Tribune](https://tribune.com.pk/story/2624677/oil-inches-up-as-trump-threatens-to-bomb-oman)
- 2026-08-04 to 08-10: WTI dropped on hopes of a deal and was about $78 on 08-10. [Tribune](https://tribune.com.pk/story/2622367/oil-prices-slip-as-iran-cites-progress-with-oman-on-hormuz-agreement)
- 2026-06-25: Prices had fallen back to pre-war levels as Middle East supply rose. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/6/25/oil-prices-back-to-pre-war-levels-on-rising-middle-east-supply)

## 4. Base rates and volatility
- One aggregator puts August 2026 WTI at roughly a $75 low and an $88 high, a range of about $12.6 in one month. Part of that data may run past 08-29, so I'm only using the range. [World Oil Monitor](https://worldoilmonitor.com/wti)
- Daily moves of $2 or more (2-3%) happened several times in late August. A weekly swing of about 4% (roughly $3.50) was seen in the week to 08-28.
- Context: In March 2026 the EIA raised its 2026 WTI forecast by $20 because of the Iran conflict. Its February forecast had been $53.42. [Rigzone](https://www.rigzone.com/news/eia_ups_wti_price_forecast_by_20_in_wake_of_iran_conflict-16-mar-2026-183215-article/?rss=true)
- With the price only about $0.40 above the threshold and typical moves of $3-8 over 8 trading days, the result is close to a coin flip on volatility alone. News about Hormuz and Iran has been the main driver.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Robinhood lists WTI prediction markets (for example, 15-minute contracts on 08-28), but I couldn't find prices for a contract on 09-10. [Robinhood](https://robinhood.com/us/en/prediction-markets/commodities/events/wti-oil-15-min-8300-target-aug-28-2026/)
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold prices for this question.
- I couldn't access the August 2026 EIA STEO, so I have no confirmed WTI forecast from it.

## 6. Upcoming events before 09-10
- U.S.-Iran diplomacy, the Iran-Oman talks on the Strait of Hormuz, and whether tanker traffic through it recovers. A reopening points down; incidents or escalation point up.
- Any follow-through on Trump's "last chance" warning to Iran.
- A possible early-September OPEC+ meeting on output. I couldn't confirm a date.
- EIA weekly petroleum status reports, around 09-02/03 and 09-09/10 (likely shifted a day by Labor Day).
- 09-07: Labor Day, U.S. markets closed.
- About 09-09: the EIA September STEO release.
- The October WTI contract is still front month on 09-10 (it expires around 09-22), so no contract-roll effect on spot is expected.
